abstract: Recently, a non-canonical role for small heat shock proteins (sHSPs) was identified, wherein sHSP-induced oligomerization drives targeted genomic accumulation of an endogenous silencing complex. Here we repurpose this property to develop sHSPs as compact, tunable tags for transcriptional engineering. Screening sHSPs across the tree of life, we show that sHSPs fused to transcription factors (TFs) can increase on-target genomic occupancy, recruit sHSP-tagged proteins, and amplify target-gene activation in mammalian cells. Distinct sHSPs vary in levels of transcriptional occupancy and output, providing a means to tune TFs activity while maintaining targeting specificity. This work establishes sHSPs as a new class of compact (~20kDa), tunable, activity-enhancing tags with broad potential for transcriptional engineering and synthetic biology.
